correctness.rationale: PASS. The T1 argument is immediate and correct: for x!=y the internal metric functional h_y separates y from a strict superlevel neighborhood of x, and h_x gives the reverse separation. On a normed space, every metric functional is a pointwise limit of convex 1-Lipschitz internal functions and hence is finite, convex and norm-continuous; each sublevel set is therefore norm-closed convex and thus weakly closed by Hahn–Banach separation. This makes every tau_diamond basic strict superlevel weakly open, proving tau_diamond subset tau_w. Walsh's horofunction result identifies extreme points of the dual unit ball with singleton Busemann metric functionals (up to the harmless sign convention); central symmetry supplies both e and -e. Since tau_diamond makes each metric functional lower semicontinuous, e and -e together make e continuous. If the extreme points algebraically span X*, every weak coordinate is therefore tau_diamond-continuous, giving the reverse inclusion. The finite-dimensional consequence follows because the span of the extreme points is a closed subspace containing the convex hull of the dual ball; strict convexity of X* makes every unit-sphere point extreme. The C[0,1] strictness argument is also valid because the source's unbounded tau_diamond-convergent sequence cannot converge weakly in a Banach space. The source's snowflake-line example supplies sharp non-Hausdorffness outside normed spaces.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. Gutiérrez–Nevanlinna introduce the topology, identify its convergent nets with d-weak convergence, and give the unbounded C[0,1] sequence; Walsh supplies the extreme-dual/Busemann identification. I found no statement in those sources of the algebraic span criterion span Ext(B_X*)=X* implying equality of topologies, nor of the resulting finite-dimensional and strictly-convex-dual topology-equality theorem. The argument is short and uses standard functional analysis once these recent ingredients are combined, so the originality claim should be read as a new synthesis/criterion rather than a deep new Banach-space theorem.

scientific_value.rationale: PASS. The criterion places a newly introduced metric-functional topology precisely relative to the classical weak topology on a broad class of normed spaces and upgrades prior sequence-level observations to equality of topologies and arbitrary-net convergence. The strict C[0,1] example shows the comparison is not tautological. Its proof is economical, but the resulting structural classification has clear conceptual value for users of the new topology.

citations.note: Gutiérrez and Nevanlinna (2026), A Weak Topology on Metric Spaces; source for tau_diamond, net convergence and the unbounded C[0,1] example.
Cormac Walsh (2018), horofunction/Busemann boundary of Banach spaces in arbitrary dimension; source for the extreme-dual singleton Busemann identification.
Gutiérrez and Nevanlinna (2026), Metric functionals and weak convergence; earlier sequence-level comparison context.

independent_checks: Re-proved T1 separation directly from internal metric functionals.
Re-proved tau_diamond subset tau_w from convex closed sublevels and Hahn–Banach separation.
Checked the finite-dimensional and strictly-convex-dual span arguments and the boundedness obstruction for C[0,1].
limitations: The extreme-span condition is sufficient and is not proved necessary.
The argument does not characterize the continuous dual of (X,tau_diamond) in general or decide equality for arbitrary C(K) spaces.
The originality is a concise synthesis of a very recent topology paper with Walsh's established horofunction theorem, so parallel independent observation is a residual risk.
